---
title: "Concepts by Type"
---

[The map](chapters/00-the-map.qmd)'s master diagram has one node per
*chapter*, colored by which of five parts that chapter belongs to —
Foundations, Objects, Structures, Theories, Applications. That's why it can
look sparse in a category like Objects: most objects (a vector, a matrix, a
random variable) are discussed *inside* a structure or theory chapter
rather than getting a page of their own, so they never became their own
node. This page is the finer-grained companion: every concept in the
[glossary](appendix-glossary.qmd), classified individually, whether or not
it has a chapter to itself.

A caveat worth stating rather than hiding: not everything below is cleanly
an object, a structure, a theory, or an application — some entries are
*properties* a structure can have (convex, bijective), *maps* between
structures (homomorphism, linear map), or *theorems* about a theory (Bayes'
rule). Forcing those into one of the four boxes would be exactly the kind
of false precision `SPEC.md`'s terminology discipline (§11) warns against,
so the **Notes** column says so explicitly instead. The five
section headings below match the map's legend exactly; the notes carry the
nuance the legend can't.

## Foundations

The substrate the object/structure/theory/application distinction is
itself built on top of — logic, sets, functions, proof. Deliberately
outside that four-way split, not a missing fifth box.

| Concept | Notes | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| Axiom | a starting statement, not a claim needing proof | [Axioms and Definitions](chapters/05-axioms-and-definitions.qmd) |
| Bijective / injective / surjective | properties of a function | [Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd) |
| Equivalence relation | a relation with three specific properties | [Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd) |
| Function | a map — see [What Is a Mathematical Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd) for why maps matter as much as objects | [Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd) |
| Logic (proposition, proof) | the inference rules everything else is checked against | [Logic and Proof](chapters/02-logic-and-proof.qmd) |
| Mathematical induction | a proof technique, introduced alongside its first real use | [Discrete Mathematics](chapters/21-discrete-mathematics.qmd) |
| Relation | the general notion underlying equality, order, and functions alike | [Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd) |
| Set | the most primitive collection — almost everything else is built from it | [Sets](chapters/03-sets.qmd) |
| Theorem | a statement derived from a theory's axioms | [Axioms and Definitions](chapters/05-axioms-and-definitions.qmd) |

## Objects

Specific instances — the level [What Is a Mathematical
Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd) uses "the matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$" to illustrate. A general vector, a
general matrix, and a general polynomial don't get their own rows below —
they're the motivating *examples* inside [Vector
Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd), not separate named concepts.

| Concept | Notes | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| Basis | a specific spanning, linearly independent set of vectors | [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd) |
| Derivative | a specific linear map (the best local approximation to $f$) | [Differentiation](chapters/18-differentiation.qmd) |
| Dimension | a number attached to a vector space | [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd) |
| Eigenvalue / eigenvector | a specific vector-and-scalar pair a linear map leaves undirected | [Linear Algebra](chapters/10-linear-algebra.qmd) |
| Embedding | a specific learned vector | [Machine Learning](chapters/24-machine-learning.qmd) |
| Entropy / KL divergence / mutual information | numbers computed from a distribution | [Machine Learning](chapters/24-machine-learning.qmd) |
| Expectation | a number computed from a random variable | [Probability](chapters/22-probability.qmd) |
| Number systems ($\mathbb{N},\mathbb{Z},\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$) | the site's one dedicated Objects chapter | [Number Systems](chapters/06-number-systems.qmd) |
| Random variable | a specific function $\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ | [Probability](chapters/22-probability.qmd) |
| Span | a specific set — all linear combinations of a given collection | [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd) |
| Zero divisor | a specific ring element | [Rings and Fields](chapters/11-rings-and-fields.qmd) |

## Structures

Sets equipped with operations or relations satisfying a fixed axiom list —
[What Is a Mathematical Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd)'s
own subject, plus the *maps between* structures of the same kind
(homomorphism, linear map, functor), grouped here rather than given a sixth
category of their own.

| Concept | Notes | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| Abelian group | a group with one extra property (commutativity) | [Groups](chapters/08-groups.qmd) |
| Affine map | a map between affine spaces (linear map + translation) | [Affine Spaces](chapters/15-affine-spaces.qmd) |
| Affine space | points and displacements, kept structurally apart | [Affine Spaces](chapters/15-affine-spaces.qmd) |
| Category | the maximal abstraction of the homomorphism pattern | [Advanced Topics](chapters/25-advanced-topics.qmd) |
| Euclidean space | affine space + inner product | [Euclidean Geometry](chapters/16-euclidean-geometry.qmd) |
| Field | a ring where every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse | [Rings and Fields](chapters/11-rings-and-fields.qmd) |
| Functor | a map between categories | [Advanced Topics](chapters/25-advanced-topics.qmd) |
| Group | one operation, four axioms | [Groups](chapters/08-groups.qmd) |
| Hilbert space | a complete inner-product space | [Advanced Topics](chapters/25-advanced-topics.qmd) |
| Homomorphism / isomorphism | maps between structures of the same kind | [What Is a Mathematical Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd) |
| Inner product / norm | angle/orthogonality, and the length it induces | [Inner Product Spaces](chapters/14-inner-product-spaces.qmd) |
| Linear map | a map between vector spaces; a matrix once bases are fixed | [Linear Algebra](chapters/10-linear-algebra.qmd) |
| Mathematical structure | the general pattern this whole section instantiates | [What Is a Mathematical Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd) |
| Metric space | a set with a distance function | [Metric Spaces](chapters/12-metric-spaces.qmd) |
| Open set | the basic building block a topology is made of | [Topological Spaces](chapters/13-topological-spaces.qmd) |
| Probability space | outcomes, events, and a probability measure | [Probability](chapters/22-probability.qmd) |
| Ring | two operations, related by distributivity | [Rings and Fields](chapters/11-rings-and-fields.qmd) |
| Topological space | a set with a designated collection of open sets | [Topological Spaces](chapters/13-topological-spaces.qmd) |
| Vector space | addition and scaling | [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd) |
| *Properties a structure can have:* completeness, orthogonal, discrete/dense, convex, continuous | not structures themselves — see each one's own chapter | — |

## Theories

The body of results about a structure or family of problems — plus the
named theorems and techniques that body of results actually produces.

| Concept | Notes | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| Bayes' rule | a theorem, not a structure | [Probability](chapters/22-probability.qmd) |
| Combinatorics | counting subsets/functions of finite sets | [Discrete Mathematics](chapters/21-discrete-mathematics.qmd) |
| Continuous | classically $\varepsilon$–$\delta$; topologically, preimages of opens | [Limits and Continuity](chapters/17-limits-and-continuity.qmd) |
| Convex / critical point | properties/objects [Optimization](chapters/23-optimization.qmd) is built around | [Optimization](chapters/23-optimization.qmd) |
| Differential Equations (ODE / PDE, dynamical system) | equations relating a function to its own derivatives | [Differential Equations](chapters/20-differential-equations.qmd) |
| Differentiation | the theory built on the derivative | [Differentiation](chapters/18-differentiation.qmd) |
| Discrete / dense | properties distinguishing $\mathbb{N},\mathbb{Z}$ from $\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R}$ | [Discrete Mathematics](chapters/21-discrete-mathematics.qmd) |
| Euclidean Geometry | affine + inner-product structure, assembled into geometry | [Euclidean Geometry](chapters/16-euclidean-geometry.qmd) |
| Functional analysis, measure theory, differential geometry, category theory | preview-depth only, per `SPEC.md` §21 | [Advanced Topics](chapters/25-advanced-topics.qmd) |
| Fundamental theorem of calculus | a theorem, not a structure | [Integration](chapters/19-integration.qmd) |
| Gradient descent | an algorithm, not a structure | [Optimization](chapters/23-optimization.qmd) |
| Independence | a property/relation between random variables | [Probability](chapters/22-probability.qmd) |
| Integration (Riemann sum) | the theory built on the integral | [Integration](chapters/19-integration.qmd) |
| Linear Algebra | the theory of vector spaces and the linear maps between them | [Linear Algebra](chapters/10-linear-algebra.qmd) |
| Probability | measure theory, wearing a specific interpretation | [Probability](chapters/22-probability.qmd) |
| Real analysis | the rigorous foundation under [Limits and Continuity](chapters/17-limits-and-continuity.qmd) | [Limits and Continuity](chapters/17-limits-and-continuity.qmd) |

## Applications

Domains that borrow a theory to solve a problem that isn't, itself,
mathematics.

| Concept | Notes | Chapter |
|---|---|---|
| Backpropagation | the chain rule, not separate mathematics | [Machine Learning](chapters/24-machine-learning.qmd) |
| Machine Learning | the site's one written Applications chapter | [Machine Learning](chapters/24-machine-learning.qmd) |
| Manifold hypothesis | [Euclidean Geometry](chapters/16-euclidean-geometry.qmd)'s manifold sketch, doing real work | [Machine Learning](chapters/24-machine-learning.qmd) |
| Physics | named throughout (Newton's laws as ODEs, symmetry and invariance) but not yet its own chapter | — *(planned)* |

## Reading this table against the map

Where a row's category surprised you, that's usually the point: a
derivative is an *object* (a specific linear map), not a theory, even
though [Differentiation](chapters/18-differentiation.qmd) — the *theory*
about derivatives in general — is a whole chapter. That gap between "the
theory" and "an instance the theory produces" is exactly what [What Is a
Mathematical Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd) spends a
full chapter making explicit, and it's the same distinction the map's
five-color legend is tracking at chapter granularity.
